tasks.title: Unpack a point
tasks.statement: You are given a tuple point with coordinates. Unpack it into variables x and y in one line and print their product.
tasks.hint: x, y = point, then print(x * y).

tasks.title: Swap the elements
tasks.statement: Write a function swap_pair(p) that takes a tuple of two elements and returns a new tuple with the elements swapped.
tasks.hint: a, b = p; return b, a. The comma in return builds a tuple.

tasks.title: Minimum and maximum
tasks.statement: Write a function min_max(nums) that returns a tuple of the smallest and the largest element of a non-empty list. It must return a tuple, not a list.

tasks.title: Division with remainder
tasks.statement: Write a function div_mod(a, b) that returns a tuple of the quotient and the remainder of dividing a by b (b is not zero). Don't use the built-in divmod: use the operators // and %.

tasks.title: Head and tail
tasks.statement: Write a function split_first(items) that returns a tuple of the first element and a list of the rest. The list is non-empty. Use unpacking with a star.

tasks.title: A board cell
tasks.statement: Write a function lookup(cells, row, col). cells is a list of tuples (row, column, value). Build a dictionary whose key is the tuple (row, column), and return the value of the cell (row, col), or None if there is no such cell.
tasks.hint: field[(r, c)] = value while building, then field.get((row, col)).

tasks.title: Oldest first
tasks.statement: Write a function sort_people(people), where people is a list of tuples (name, age). Return a new list sorted by age from oldest to youngest, and for equal ages, by name alphabetically. The sort key is the tuple (minus age, name).
tasks.hint: def by_key(person): name, age = person; return -age, name.
